title: How glaciers carve U-shaped valleys
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How does a glacier carve a valley?

explain.say: In cold mountains, more snow falls each winter than melts each summer. Over years, the weight of new snow presses the old snow into thick, solid ice: a glacier.

explain.say: The ice is so heavy that gravity makes it flow slowly downhill, like extremely thick toothpaste, usually a few centimetres to metres a day.

explain.say: As it moves, the ice freezes onto rocks and rips them out, called plucking. Those rocks, frozen into the base, scrape the valley floor like sandpaper, called abrasion.

explain.say: A river cuts a narrow V-shaped valley, but a glacier fills the whole valley and grinds its sides and floor, making it deep, wide and U-shaped. When the ice melts, the U-shape is left.

faq.a: Gravity pulls the heavy ice downhill. The ice slowly bends and flows inside, and it also slides over its bed on a thin layer of meltwater. Most glaciers move a few centimetres to a few metres a day.
By plucking, when ice freezes onto rock and tears it away as it moves, and by abrasion, when rocks stuck in the ice scrape and polish the ground beneath like giant sandpaper.
A glacier fills the whole valley, so it grinds the sides as well as the floor. That widens and deepens the valley into a U-shape with steep sides and a flat bottom.
asks: What is the difference between a V-shaped and a U-shaped valley?

faq.a: A small side valley that was carved less deeply than the main glacier valley. After the ice melts it is left high above the main valley, often with a waterfall pouring out.
asks: Why do waterfalls drop from side valleys?

faq.q: Where can I see glacial valleys?
faq.a: In mountains that had glaciers in the last ice age, like Yosemite Valley in the USA, the Lake District in England and the Alps.

facts: Yosemite Valley in California is a famous U-shaped valley carved by glaciers.
Glacier ice forms from snow compressed over many years.

quiz.say: What shape of valley does a glacier usually carve?
quiz.why: A glacier fills the valley and grinds its sides and floor, leaving a wide U-shape.

wrong.1: V-shaped valleys are cut by rivers.
wrong.2: Glaciers do carve bowls called corries at their heads, but whole valleys become U-shaped.
